land.text: Masovia proper and eastern Kuyavia, the share of Bolesław IV the Curly under the 1138 testament

predecessors.note: 'It was formed in 1138 from the territories of the Kingdom of Poland'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1138.

land.text: Masovia as Cliopatria draws it in its last year; the Kingdom of Poland shape of 1352 covers 131 of its 132 cells

successors.note: 'in 1351 he and his brother Casimir became vassals of the Polish kings'. The Masovian Piast dukes kept the duchy until 'the male line of the Masovian Piasts became extinct upon the death of ... Janusz III in 1526', when 'the country was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland'; Cliopatria hands the land to its Kingdom of Poland row from 1352 and to the House of Jagiellon later, so the vassal duchy of 1351-1526 is not drawn here (see notes).

capitals.name: Płock
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Płock' without dates; the Konrad I page has 'Płock Castle' as his residence. The start year is the duchy's; the end is the year before the infobox's 'Czersk (from 1262)'. Coordinates are the town's, not from the page.

capitals.name: Czersk
capitals.note: Infobox 'Czersk (from 1262)'; 'Duke Konrad II (1264-1294) moved his residence to Czersk'. After 1313 the sons of Bolesław II divided Masovia (Rawa, Czersk, Płock), and Warsaw became the residence in 1413 (outside the dossier). Coordinates are approximate (the old town near Góra Kalwaria).

rulers.name: Bolesław IV the Curly
rulers.note: 'Duke of Masovia and Kuyavia 1138-1173'; High Duke of Poland 1146-1173; died 5 January 1173.

rulers.name: Leszek of Masovia
rulers.note: 'succeeded ... in the Masovian-Kujavian principality by his second and only surviving son, Leszek'; 'In 1186, Duke Leszek of Masovia died' (Casimir II page).

rulers.name: Casimir II the Just
rulers.note: Infobox 'Duke of Masovia, 1186-1194': 'Casimir could only take possession of Masovia proper'; he died on 5 May 1194.

rulers.name: Konrad I
rulers.note: Infobox '1194-1247: Konrad I'; the Konrad I page: 'After his father's death in 1194, Konrad was brought up by his mother, who acted as regent of Masovia' and 'In 1199, he received Masovia'; died 31 August 1247. High Duke 1229-1232 and 1241-1243.

rulers.name: Siemowit I
rulers.note: Infobox '1248-1262: Siemowit I'; 'Masovia passed to the first-born Bolesław I upon his death in 1247' (Bolesław I's reign is not dated on the pages opened).

rulers.name: Konrad II
rulers.note: 'Konrad II (1264-1294)' moved his residence to Czersk. Gaps 1262-1264 and 1294-1313 (Bolesław II, 'Upon the death of Duke Boleslaus II in 1313') are not dated on the pages opened; after 1313 the sons ruled Rawa, Czersk and Płock separately (Siemowit III 1341-1381).

rulers.name: Bolesław II
rulers.note: Infobox 'Duke of Masovia 1294-1313': 'In 1294 Konrad II died without male offspring, so Bolesław II became the sole ruler over all Masovia'; he had ruled Płock from 1275 ('Duke of Masovia during 1262-1275 jointly with his brother, after 1275 sole ruler over Płock'); 'In 1310 he gave to his sons the districts of Warsaw and Czersk'; died 20 April 1313. Successors Siemowit II and Trojden I; the 1313-1351 strip is not dated on the pages opened.

correction.text: Masovia unchanged by the Mongol raid, with Kraków's Lesser Poland, 1241-1242

keyframe_review.note: 1241-1249, 29,260 km2 (129 cells, 11 fewer than 1236: lon 20.8-22.2E, lat 51.7-52.1N, which Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row holds in 1241-1249). The page records a raid ('invaded the Duchy of Sandomierz in the winter of 1240-1241', Sandomierz sacked on 13 February, Kraków seized by 24 March, Legnica on 9 April), never names Masovia, Płock or Konrad, says the Mongols 'did not take Legnica Castle' and that Ögedei's death 'probably saved the Polish lands from being completely overrun'; for 1259 'Berke had no intention of occupying or conquering Poland'. No page opened shows Mongol rule over Masovian land for 1241-1249, so the 1236 shape is kept (a reading from silence: the page does not mention Masovia). [Repair 2026-10-31] Valid 1241-1242 with Lesser Poland (Konrad enters Kraków on 10 July 1241 and loses it on 25 May 1243); 1243 onward in the next keyframes.

Masovia without the Dobrzyń Land, 1333-1343 (the Dobrzyń Land is Poland's, then the Order's by conquest, never Masovia's since 1248)

keyframe_review.note: 1333-1343, 25,854 km2 (112 cells, 20 fewer than 1326; Cliopatria gives 21 of the 22 lost cells to its Teutonic Order row in 1333-1343). 'During the Polish-Teutonic War of 1326-1332, the forces of the Order's State occupied Dobrzyń Land' and the land was 'relinquished to the Kingdom of Poland in the 1343 Treaty of Kalisz'. Only the Dobrzyń Land (8 of the 22 cells, within 32 km of 53.0N 19.4E) is on the pages; the other 14 cells, a band from Sochaczew (20.1E) through Płock and Sierpc to Mława, have no page and are restored to Masovia. Valid 1333-1342. [Repair 2026-10-31] Valid 1333-1343 (was 1333-1342); the Dobrzyń Land is out for the reason of the 1248 loss, not because the Order took it from Masovia.

correction.text: Masovia without the Dobrzyń Land, which the Treaty of Kalisz gave to Poland, 1344-1351

keyframe_review.note: 1344-1351, 30,989 km2 (132 cells, the 1326 shape again). The Dobrzyń Land page: the land 'was relinquished to the Kingdom of Poland in the 1343 Treaty of Kalisz', not to Masovia; the Dobrzyń cells (8) are taken out for 1343-1351 (the Kingdom of Poland dossier should hold them; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape does not draw them). 'in 1351 he and his brother Casimir became vassals of the Polish kings' (Masovia page). [Repair 2026-10-31] Dobrzyń is out of Masovia since 1248 (Casimir I of Kuyavia).

ledger.note: 1138: Bolesław III's testament creates the Duchy of Masovia for Bolesław IV the Curly. 'It was formed in 1138 from the territories of the Kingdom of Poland'; the Testament page: 'Masovia proper and eastern Kuyavia'.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province, Silesia and the Łęczyca land: the part of Cliopatria's 1147 shape outside Masovia proper

ledger.note: 1146: Bolesław IV the Curly becomes High Duke and takes the Seniorate and Silesia. 'High Duke of Poland from 1146 until his death in 1173'; the page says the Duchy of Silesia and the Seniorate Province at Kraków went to Bolesław in the 1146 reassignment ('Duke of Silesia 1146-1163'); Łęczyca had reverted to the Seniorate in 1144. Władysław II 'was eventually defeated and expelled from Poland in 1146' (Testament page).

1163: Silesia returns to Władysław II's sons. 'Not before 1163, the sons of the late Władysław' were 'restored in their Silesia heritage' (table: 'Duke of Silesia 1146-1163'); Testament page: 'his sons managed to retain the Silesian Province in 1163'.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province as Bolesław IV held them 1169-1172, without Silesia (restored 1163), Sandomierz Land and Leszek's Masovia and Kuyavia: the 1169-1172 shape minus the 1173-1176 Masovian shape

ledger.note: January 1173: Bolesław IV dies and Mieszko III takes the Seniorate. 'Died: 5 January 1173'; 'he however was succeeded by his next brother Mieszko III the Old' as High Duke, while Leszek succeeded 'in the Masovian-Kujavian principality'; Casimir II got Sandomierz (Casimir II page). [Repair 2026-10-31: the region was the 1146 shape, which holds Silesia (already returned in 1163) and Kuyavia (Leszek's); the Greater Poland dossier's 1173 gain uses the same land minus Cliopatria's Kuyavia cells.]

1186: Leszek of Masovia dies; Casimir II takes Masovia proper and Mieszko III Kuyavia. 'In 1186, Duke Leszek of Masovia died.' 'Casimir could only take possession of Masovia proper'; 'Mieszko III occupied the lands of Kuyavia up to the Vistula River'.

region.text: the lands of Kuyavia up to the Vistula River (Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia row)

ledger.note: 1186: Mieszko III of Greater Poland occupies Kuyavia 'up to the Vistula River' on Leszek's death.
1199: Konrad I receives Masovia. 'In 1199, he received Masovia' (infobox 'Reign: 1194-1247'; after 1194 his mother acted as regent). Masovia proper had been Casimir II's since 1186.

region.text: the adjacent lands of Kuyavia (Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia row, 29 cells)

ledger.note: 1205: Konrad I adds Kuyavia. 'in 1205, the adjacent lands of Kuyavia as well.' The Greater Poland page puts the cession of Kuyavia to Konrad in 1199 and the Mieszko III page in 1198 to 'Casimir's sons'; Cliopatria has a separate Duchy of Kuyavia row to 1205. The Greater Poland dossier's ledger 11 now hands Kuyavia in 1199 to duchy-of-kuyavia (Cliopatria's row, 1188-1205), so Cliopatria's Kuyavia row holds the land 1199-1205 and this 1205 gain mirrors it.

region.text: Kraków and Lesser Poland, the High Duke's seat; the Konrad I page names no land for the title

ledger.note: 1229: Konrad I takes the title of High Duke. He 'assumed the title of a Polish High Duke in 1229' in his dispute with Spindleshanks (infobox 'Reign: 1229-1232'); Odonic and Konrad acted together against Spindleshanks. The Seniorate is the land by reading. [Repair 2026-10-31: the region was the 1146 shape (Seniorate, Silesia, Łęczyca: 553 cells, 123 of them in Cliopatria's Silesia row), which gave Konrad Silesia, Henry the Bearded's land; now Kraków's Lesser Poland, as in the war zone and the Silesia dossier's 1232 gain. The Greater Poland dossier's matching 1229 loss names the wider Seniorate it drew in 1228.]

region.text: the Chełmno Land (Kulmerland) and the adjoining lands north of the Dobrzyń Land: 19 cells

ledger.note: 1230: Konrad cedes the Chełmno Land to the Teutonic Order. 'he was the ruler who in 1226 called the Teutonic Order for help against the pagan Old Prussians. In turn he ceded the Prussian Chełmno Land (Kulmerland) to the knights in 1230.' Cliopatria's Teutonic Order row holds the cells from 1236.

region.text: Kraków and Lesser Poland, the High Duke's seat; the Konrad I page names no land for the title

ledger.note: 1232: Henry I the Bearded of Silesia becomes High Duke at Kraków. The Konrad I page says Henry I the Bearded 'finally prevailed as High Duke at Kraków in 1232'; Konrad's infobox 'Reign: 1229-1232'. [Repair 2026-10-31: region narrowed to Lesser Poland, as for the 1229 gain; it matches the Silesia dossier's ledger 13. The Silesia dossier names duchy-of-greater-poland as the holder it takes Kraków from; the Konrad I page makes it Konrad.]

1233: Konrad gives Kuyavia to his son. 'In 1233 Konrad gave Kujawy to his second son Casimir I' (infobox 'Split off Kuyavia: 1233'). Cliopatria has no Kuyavia row after 1205. The Casimir I of Kuyavia page: 'Casimir I received Kujawy (however, without Dobrzyń) from his father in 1233', so the Dobrzyń Land stays Masovian until 1248 (ledger below).

region.text: the Radom district, 30 km round Radom (21.15E 51.40N, the town's coordinates; the gazetteer lacks Radom)

ledger.note: 1235: Konrad of Masovia takes the Radom district. 'In June 1235, Pope Gregory IX approved the Treaty of Luchani; however, shortly afterwards, Konrad invaded Sandomierz, and as a result of this invasion, Bolesław lost the district of Radom.' Mirrors duchy-of-sandomierz ledger 17. Radom lies south of every Cliopatria Masovia shape, so it is added to the keyframes 1235-1238.

9 July 1239: Konrad gives up on Sandomierz at Przedbórz. 'On 9 July of that year, a meeting also took place in Przedbórz between Bolesław and Konrad, at which the Masovian ruler agreed to renounce his claims over Sandomierz.' The page does not say Radom was handed back; the Sandomierz dossier (ledger 18, also confidence 1) reads it so. Mirrors that event.

10 July 1241: Konrad I enters Kraków. Bolesław V page: Konrad 'finally entered Kraków on 10 July 1241'; the Konrad I infobox lists his second High Duke reign as 'Reign: 1241-1243'. Mirrors duchy-of-silesia ledger 23 (loss of Kraków to Masovia on 10 July 1241, after Henry II's fall at Legnica). The land is Lesser Poland by reading.

25 May 1243: Bolesław V wins Kraków at Suchodoły. 'On 25 May of that year, the Battle of Suchodoły took place' (the page's year is 1243); the Masovian troops of Konrad were defeated and 'Bolesław the Chaste regained the government over Kraków'. Mirrors duchy-of-sandomierz ledger 21 (gain). Replaces the contest_start/contest_end pair of 1241-1243: Konrad held Kraków, so it is a gain and a loss.

region.text: the Dobrzyń Land: Masovia's 1236 shape within 32 km of 53.0N 19.4E (8 cells)

ledger.note: 1248: Casimir I of Kuyavia takes the Dobrzyń Land from his brother's heirs. 'The next geopolitical change in Masovia came in early 1248, when Bolesław I died unexpectedly and without issue'; Casimir 'was able to take advantage of the confusion after his older brother's death and capture Dobrzyń'; infobox 'Duke of Dobrzyń after 1248' (the body gives no year for the capture itself). The Dobrzyń Land page: 'During the whole second half of the 13th century it belonged to the Kuyavian Piasts'. Replaces the 1332 loss to the Teutonic Order (removed): the Order took the land from Poland (teutonic-order ledger 10), not from Masovia. Casimir I's duchy is not in Cliopatria (counterpart needing a dossier).
1262: the dukes' seat moves from Płock to Czersk. Infobox 'Czersk (from 1262)'; 'Duke Konrad II (1264-1294) moved his residence to Czersk'.

region.text: two cells at 22.2-22.3E 52.4-52.5N on the eastern edge

ledger.note: 1326: a strip on the north-eastern edge goes to Lithuania. The page: 'a short conflict' between Lithuania and the Masovian dukes 'after the 1326 Brodnica agreement'; it names no land, so the year and the 2 cells Cliopatria moves are a bridge. Reopened for the repair pass: the Wenceslaus of Płock page names no land lost to Lithuania in 1326 (it has only the Polish-Teutonic War), so the strip stays a confidence-1 reading of Cliopatria's two cells.

region.text: Masovia as Cliopatria draws it in its last year

ledger.note: 1351: the Masovian dukes become vassals of the Polish king. 'in 1351 he and his brother Casimir became vassals of the Polish kings'. The duchy lasted to 1526 ('In 1526, the country was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland'); the dissolve is the map boundary: Cliopatria gives the land to its Kingdom of Poland row from 1352.

wars.name: Polish campaign of Frederick Barbarossa (1157)
wars.outcome: Bolesław IV was 'declared a vassal of the Empire at his camp in Krzyszkowo' on 30 August 1157, begged forgiveness on his knees and 'had to pay an enormous tribute'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: 'Bolesław formally swore loyalty to the Emperor on Christmas Day in Magdeburg' (year not stated). Cliopatria draws no Empire-vassal relation for these years.

wars.name: Bolesław IV's Prussian campaign
wars.outcome: 'efforts and attempts to conquer these provinces were finally defeated in 1166'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Konrad I's wars with the Old Prussians
wars.outcome: 'Several further campaigns in 1219, 1222 failed'; in 1226 Konrad called the Teutonic Order and in 1230 ceded the Chełmno Land to the knights.
wars.note: The Dobrzyń Order (1228) was 'soon absorbed by the Teutonic Knights' (Dobrzyń Land page); the Treaty of Kruszwica (1230) is probably a forgery (Konrad I page).

wars.name: Konrad I's bid for the High Duchy (1229-1232)
wars.outcome: Konrad took the title of High Duke in 1229 against Spindleshanks and held it to 1232, when Henry I the Bearded prevailed at Kraków.

wars.name: Konrad I's invasion of Sandomierz (1235-1239)
wars.outcome: After the Treaty of Luchani Konrad invaded Sandomierz and Bolesław V lost the Radom district (1235); at Przedbórz on 9 July 1239 Konrad renounced his claims over Sandomierz.
wars.note: The Konrad I page is silent on all of it.

wars.name: Konrad I's second bid for Kraków (1241-1243)
wars.outcome: Konrad entered Kraków on 10 July 1241 (Bolesław V page; infobox High Duke 1241-1243) and Bolesław V regained it at Suchodoły on 25 May 1243.
wars.note: The Konrad I page does not mention Kraków for 1241 or the fighting of 1243; the dates come from the Bolesław V page.

wars.name: First Mongol invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: Sandomierz sacked on 13 February 1241, Kraków seized by 24 March, Legnica on 9 April; the Mongols left and 'Ögedei's death probably saved the Polish lands from being completely overrun'.
wars.note: The page does not mention Masovia; Cliopatria draws 11 Masovian cells as Mongol Empire in 1241-1249, which the keyframe review returns to Masovia.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: 'Duke Wenceslaus of Płock' was an ally of the Order; the Order 'pillaged and conquered the Polish Kuyavian region and the Dobrzyń Land'; the Treaty of Kalisz (1343) returned the Dobrzyń Land to Poland. The Dobrzyń Land had been Casimir I of Kuyavia's since 1248 (Casimir I of Kuyavia page), so the Order took it from Poland, not from Masovia.
wars.note: The page gives 1326-1327 as the start and is silent on 1329, Bohemian homage, and the Masovian dukes other than Wenceslaus of Płock.

wars.name: Lithuanian-Masovian conflict of 1326

zones.text: two cells on the eastern edge

wars.outcome: A short conflict between Poland's ally Lithuania and the Masovian dukes after the 1326 Brodnica agreement between Trojden I and the Teutonic Order.
wars.note: The page names no land or result; the zone is Cliopatria's 2-cell change.

certainty.note: A duchy of castellany districts with Prussian, Yotvingian and Rus' marches: no page opened gives a surveyed or treaty boundary. The Chełmno cession of 1230 rests on a Golden Bull of 1226 and a Treaty of Kruszwica that is probably forged; the Dobrzyń line is that of the 1343 Treaty of Kalisz; every other frontier is approximate.

notes: eu-15-d, Duchy of Masovia. 18 Cliopatria shapes (1139-1351) all reviewed with nine content pages (plus one disambiguation page); no infobox area exists, so no area comparison was possible. Cliopatria uses this row for three things: Masovia proper (35 thousand km2, 1139-1146, 1177-1187, 1202-1351), the High Duke's Seniorate realm of Bolesław IV (166 and 156 thousand km2, 1147-1176: the 1147 shape is, to within four cells, the Silesia 1139 shape plus Masovia plus Łęczyca, the 1169 shape is the same without Silesia but with Sandomierz Land), and a gap 1188-1201 that its Sandomierz row covers. The Seniorate years are page-based (1146 gain, 1163 Silesia loss, 1173 loss to Mieszko III) and the new keyframes 1146, 1163, 1173 follow them. Pages silent or short: Konrad I (nothing on 1233, 1235 Radom, 1239 Przedbórz, the 1243 battle; the Sandomierz dossier records Radom lost 1235 and regained 1239 and a 1241-1243 contest and its pairing events are mirrored only for 1241-1243); the Masovia page (no Bohemian suzerainty 1329, no Yotvingian or Rus' lands, no dates for Dobrzyń/Płock/Wizna); Cliopatria's 1250 trim (7 cells) and the 1279/1305 one-cell changes have no page (ok, unverified: page budget). Disagreements between pages: Kuyavia to Konrad in 1198 (Mieszko III), 1199 (Greater Poland) or 1205 (Konrad I); the Mongol raid versus Cliopatria's 8 years of Mongol cells; the Dobrzyń Land held by the Kuyavian Piasts (Dobrzyń page) versus drawn as Masovian in every Cliopatria shape to 1332 [resolved in the repair pass: out of Masovia from 1248]; Cliopatria's Teutonic cells of 1333-1343 (21 cells in a band from Sochaczew to Mława) versus the pages' Dobrzyń Land alone (8 cells): the other 14 cells are restored. Events at confidence 1: 1326 (Lithuania), 1332 (Dobrzyń). The vassal duchy of 1351-1526 (Janusz III d. 1526; the 1413 Warsaw residence; Belz until 1462) is not drawn: Cliopatria hands the land to Kingdom of Poland and the House of Jagiellon; eu-15-x or the Kingdom of Poland dossier should record the vassal tint (vassal_start 1351, vassal_end 1526, counterpart duchy-of-masovia) and the separate dukes of Rawa, Czersk and Płock after 1313. Counterparts needing dossiers: Duchy of Kuyavia of Casimir I (1233-1267, not in Cliopatria; the existing duchy-of-kuyavia row is 1188-1205), the Dobrzyń Land, Old Prussians, Duchy of Płock. Names the gazetteer lacks: Płock, Czersk, Dobrzyń Land, Chełmno Land, Sochaczew (the Dobrzyń Land is a 32 km circle at 19.4E 53.0N; the other regions are Cliopatria references). REPAIR PASS 2026-10-31 (reviewer fixes, pages reopened): (1) The 1229 gain and 1232 loss now name Lesser Poland (Kraków), not the 1146 shape, which held Silesia; keyframes 1229-1231 draw Masovia, Kuyavia and Lesser Poland (the old keyframe 1227 is split at 1229, 1230 at 1232). The Greater Poland dossier's 1229 loss still names the wider Seniorate it drew in 1228 (353 cells), so Łódź, Łęczyca and the rest of that region are drawn by nobody in 1229-1231: the pages name no holder. The Silesia dossier's 1232 gain names duchy-of-greater-poland, not this duchy. (2) The 1173 loss now uses keyframe 1169-1172 minus keyframe 1173-1176 (no Silesia, no Kuyavia). (3) 1241/7 gain of Kraków from Silesia and 1243/5 loss to Sandomierz replace the contest pair (Bolesław V page: 'he finally entered Kraków on 10 July 1241'; 'On 25 May of that year [1243], the Battle of Suchodoły took place'; 'Bolesław the Chaste regained the government over Kraków'), with keyframes 1241-1242. (4) Dobrzyń Land: Casimir I of Kuyavia got Kujawy 'without Dobrzyń' in 1233 and captured it after Bolesław I's death in 'early 1248' (Casimir I of Kuyavia page; the body gives no year for the capture itself, the infobox says 'Duke of Dobrzyń after 1248'); the Dobrzyń page has it with the Kuyavian Piasts 'the whole second half of the 13th century'. The 1332 loss to the Order (confidence 1) is deleted: teutonic-order ledger 10 has the Order take it from kingdom-of-poland, and the 8 cells are out of every keyframe from 1248. (5) Kuyavia: the Greater Poland dossier now hands Kuyavia in 1199 to duchy-of-kuyavia (Cliopatria's row); this dossier's 1205 gain from duchy-of-kuyavia mirrors it; the 1199-1205 disagreement between the pages (Greater Poland: 1199 to Konrad; Konrad I: 1205) remains in both notes. (6) Radom: a 1235 gain and a 9 July 1239 loss (confidence 1; the page does not say Radom was handed back) now mirror the Sandomierz dossier, with keyframes 1235-1238 holding the Radom circle. Still open: the one-to-seven-cell changes of 1250, 1279 and 1305 (unverified: page budget), the 1326 Lithuanian strip (the Wenceslaus of Płock page names no land), and the ruler strip 1313-1351. Rulers: Bolesław II 1294-1313 added from his page. Counterpart needing a dossier: the Kuyavian duchy of Casimir I (1233-1267), which also holds the Dobrzyń Land from 1248.
